research_concepts: teammate gain in primary play types
methodological_questions: defining and computing pre-absence initiation profile similarity
measuring 'largest gainer in the absent player's primary types'
handling very small number of absence spells (n=148 spells, only 11 cases)
confounding by minutes changes, role assignment, and opponent adjustments
reliability of play-type classification and spectrum boundaries

historical_evidence.finding: Having a similar-profile teammate does not separate absorption from cascade when a player sits. Mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(similarity, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 23-24 cascades with Reed similarity 0.94. Verdict: null (adequately powered null result).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using pre-absence initiation similarity to predict whether the absent player's initiations are absorbed by a single teammate or cascade across the team.
failed_approaches.why: Similarity scores were almost always findable, and did not separate absorb from cascade; Spearman correlation was wrong-signed, indicating no positive relationship. The failure was judged adequately powered.

evidence_establishes: Pre-absence initiation profile similarity does not distinguish absorption from cascade (SF-CHT-052).
Similarity metrics alone are not predictive of how the team redistributes initiations when a player sits.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether other proximity measures (minutes, same-position minutes, raw initiation counts) would predict the largest gainer in primary types.
Whether the 'largest gainer' outcome is inherently different from absorption/cascade patterns.
Whether the effect could be detected with a larger sample or better-specified outcome classes.
own_inferences: The current question is essentially a finer-grained version of the similarity-prediction hypothesis that already returned a powered null (SF-CHT-052).
With only 11 qualifying cases, even a moderate effect is undetectable; the test is severely underpowered.
The high similarity values in the prior study suggest that 'closest' profile is often trivially close, making the predictor nearly constant and unable to discriminate.
uncertainties: Exact definition of initiation profile and distance metric not standardized; prior work used cosine similarity on play-type vectors.
What constitutes 'primary types' for an absent player: threshold-based or top-N, and how stable they are pre-absence.
Selection mechanism of absences: non-random, often injury/load management, which may coincide with lineup changes that confound teammate gain.
Whether protection of the absent player's role by coach instruction overrides inherent similarity effects.

historical_effect.explanation: SF-CHT-052 demonstrates a null result for a closely related question (similarity predicting replacement concentration). Without this evidence, one might have assumed that similarity is a plausible driver and designed a study around the 11 cases. The null, together with the tiny sample, strongly argues against a testable positive result.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence cases are available for the proposed question; even a large effect would require far more spells to achieve acceptable power.
Primary play types may have few initiations per player, making within-spell gain estimates unstable.
Initiation profile similarity depends on play-type classification boundaries; prior work shows these can be noisy.
The teammate who gains most may be the one whose minutes increase most, not the most similar; similarity and minutes changes are collinear.

prior_work.summary: SF-CHT-052 tested whether pre-absence similarity in initiation profiles predicts absorb vs. cascade. It found no signal (powered null). The current question extends similarity to predict the single largest gainer in primary types, a more granular outcome, but the fundamental predictor-outcome link was already null.

risks.text: Only 11 cases available; the test would be too underpowered to detect any realistic effect.
Primary play types may be rare; zero-inflated gain measures would violate distributional assumptions.
Initiation profile similarity computed from play-type vectors is sensitive to classification thresholds and spectrum edges.
Misclassification of play types or initiator assignment (e.g., shared possessions) could distort similarity and gain measures.
Coaching decisions, opponent matchups, and minutes adjustments may determine gain independently of profile similarity.
If testing across multiple absence types or play types, multiplicity would further degrade power.

design.estimand: Difference in gain (change in initiations per 100 possessions) in the absent player's top-3 primary play types between the teammate most similar in pre-absence initiation profile and the average of the next two most-similar teammates, within the same absence spell.
design.unit: absence spell, with each spell defined as a continuous set of games missed by one player (team-season).
design.sample: All spells in 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons where: (1) the absent player has >=400 total on-court possessions in the same season prior to the spell, (2) at least two teammates also have >=200 pre-absence possessions, (3) the absent player has a defined primary play type set (top-3 by share) with >=30 initiations each pre-absence, (4) the spell covers >=2 games, and (5) the teammates' similarity ranks can be computed. Expected sample: 11 spells; far below required.
design.power: Simulation indicates that to detect a Cohen's d=0.8 (large) with 80% power at alpha=0.05, N=15 spells would be needed just for a paired t-test. For a more complex model with covariates, N>=40 would be required. The available 11 spells yield <50% power even for large effects.
design.controls: No adjustments planned due to severe overfitting risk; in a minimally viable test one would condition on delta-minutes of the most-similar teammate, opponent defensive rating, and home/road, requiring many more degrees of freedom.
design.falsification: Placebo test: use pre-absence similarity measures computed from seasons other than the current one (e.g., previous season) to see if they still predict gain; if they do, confounding is present. Not feasible with 11 spells.
design.multiplicity: If testing multiple definitions of 'closest' and 'primary types,' a Bonferroni adjustment would be applied, further reducing power.
design.decision_rule: Bayesian posterior probability with a skeptical prior (normal(0,0.2)); reject if 95% credible interval for the gain difference excludes zero. Not intended to be used due to decision to not proceed.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 complete seasons as of 2026-11-01.

methodological_questions: measuring gain in play type initiations
identifying the teammate who gains most
controlling for minutes changes and position
sample size and sparsity of absence spells
